subject: art-design
title: Printmaking Methods: Application
welcome_lead: Apply lino, drypoint and screen-print processes step by step.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE printmaking: lino cutting, drypoint etching, screen printing, monoprint.
final_note: Process discipline is what makes editions consistent.

concepts.def: Intaglio line scratched into a plate.
Raised metal edge of a drypoint scratch.
Ink pushed through a mesh stencil.
A single one-off impression that cannot repeat.
Roller used to apply ink evenly to a block.

walkthroughs.body_html: Transfer the design in reverse. Cut away the white areas with gouges, always cutting away from your fingers. Ink the surface with a brayer, lay paper on top, burnish or press, then peel back. Repeat for an edition.

Scratch a needle directly into a metal or acetate plate. The burr — the raised curl beside each scratch — catches extra ink and gives a soft, dark line. Wipe surface ink, leaving ink in the grooves, then press into damp paper.

Screen print uses a stretched mesh blocked off in negative areas — by paper stencil or photo emulsion. Pull a squeegee across to push ink through the open mesh onto paper. Great for bold colour layers like Warhol's pop-art works.
